title: Microsoft 365 Fundamentals
subtitle: 20 questions across cloud concepts, M365 apps, identity, compliance, and licensing

questions.q: Microsoft 365 is best classified as which cloud service model?
questions.note: M365 delivers ready-to-use apps over the internet - the definition of SaaS.

explain.correct: Microsoft 365 delivers fully managed productivity applications over the internet, which is the definition of SaaS. Microsoft manages everything from infrastructure to the application layer.
wrong: IaaS provides virtualized compute, storage, and networking (e.g., Azure VMs) - not finished applications like Word or Teams.
PaaS provides a development platform for building apps (e.g., Azure App Service) - not end-user productivity software.
FaaS (serverless functions) is a subset of PaaS for event-driven code execution - not a productivity suite like M365.

questions.q: Under the shared responsibility model in Microsoft 365, which of the following is the CUSTOMER's responsibility?
questions.note: Microsoft secures the infrastructure; customers own identity, data, devices, and access.

explain.correct: In the SaaS shared responsibility model, customers are responsible for securing identities (accounts, MFA, access policies), their data, and their endpoints - Microsoft handles everything below that.
wrong: Physical datacenter security (locks, guards, hardware) is always Microsoft's responsibility in a cloud model.
Network infrastructure patching is part of the infrastructure layer that Microsoft owns and maintains.
Hypervisor security is Microsoft's responsibility - customers never touch the virtualization layer in SaaS.

questions.q: What is the default OneDrive for Business storage quota per user in Microsoft 365?
questions.note: OneDrive for Business starts at 1 TB per user by default.

explain.correct: OneDrive for Business provides 1 TB of storage per user by default across most M365 plans.
wrong: 100 GB is the Exchange Online mailbox size on E3/E5 plans - not OneDrive default storage.
500 GB is not a current OneDrive for Business default quota in any standard M365 plan.
5 TB is available after an admin grants additional storage, but is not the default starting quota.

questions.q: A user enables OneDrive 'Files On-Demand.' What happens to files that have NOT been opened yet?
options: They are deleted from OneDrive after 30 days
They appear as placeholders and download only when opened
They are compressed and stored locally
questions.note: Files On-Demand shows placeholder icons - actual data downloads only when you click to open the file.

explain.correct: Files On-Demand displays cloud-only placeholder files in File Explorer. The full file content downloads to the local disk only when the user opens the file, saving local storage.
wrong: Files On-Demand never deletes cloud content - files remain in OneDrive indefinitely until manually deleted.
Files On-Demand does not compress files locally - it simply defers download until access.
Files On-Demand is a local sync behavior - it does not trigger automatic migration to SharePoint.

questions.q: Where are files attached or shared in a Microsoft Teams CHANNEL stored?
questions.note: Every Teams channel is backed by a SharePoint document library - files posted there live in SharePoint.

explain.correct: Each Microsoft Teams channel automatically creates a corresponding folder in a SharePoint Online document library. Files shared in a channel are stored in SharePoint.
wrong: OneDrive for Business stores files shared in Teams private CHATS (1:1 and group chats) - not channel files.
Exchange Online stores Teams chat MESSAGES and meeting data - not the file attachments.
Azure Blob Storage is a developer-facing object store - Teams does not use it for end-user file storage.

questions.q: How many devices can a single user install Microsoft 365 Apps on?
questions.note: M365 Apps licenses allow installs on up to 5 PCs/Macs + 5 tablets + 5 phones per user.

explain.correct: A single Microsoft 365 Apps license allows each user to install the full Office desktop apps on up to 5 PCs or Macs, 5 tablets, and 5 smartphones simultaneously.
wrong: The 3-device limit applies to older Office 2016 volume licensing - not modern Microsoft 365 subscriptions.
There is no 10-device or unlimited-mobile tier in standard M365 Apps licensing.
A 1+1 device limit has not existed for M365 Apps - the model has always been designed for multi-device users.

questions.q: Which Microsoft 365 plan is the ONLY one that includes Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2, Teams Phone System, AND Power BI Pro?
questions.note: E5 is the top enterprise tier and uniquely bundles Defender P2, Phone System, and Power BI Pro.

explain.correct: Microsoft 365 E5 is the only plan that includes all three: Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 (advanced EDR + threat intelligence), Teams Phone System (cloud PSTN calling), and Power BI Pro (self-service analytics).
wrong: Business Premium includes Defender for Business (not Defender for Endpoint P2) and lacks Phone System and Power BI Pro.
E3 includes Defender for Endpoint P1 and Intune but does not include Phone System or Power BI Pro.
F3 (Frontline) targets deskless workers and does not include Defender for Endpoint P2, Phone System, or Power BI Pro.

questions.q: Which Entra ID feature evaluates signals like user location, device compliance, and app being accessed to decide whether to grant or block access?
questions.note: Conditional Access is the if/then policy engine - it evaluates signals and enforces access decisions.

explain.correct: Conditional Access is an if/then policy engine in Entra ID (P1 or higher required). It evaluates signals such as user identity, location, device state, and application, then enforces actions like requiring MFA or blocking access.
wrong: MFA is an authentication method (one factor of the decision) - it does not evaluate signals or make policy-based access decisions on its own.
PIM (Privileged Identity Management) provides just-in-time activation of admin roles - it does not evaluate per-access signals for normal users.
Identity Protection detects risk events (risky sign-ins, leaked credentials) and can feed signals INTO Conditional Access, but it is not the policy engine itself.

questions.q: According to Microsoft, enabling Multi-Factor Authentication blocks approximately what percentage of account-compromise attacks?
questions.note: Microsoft research shows MFA blocks roughly 99.9% of automated account-compromise attacks.

explain.correct: Microsoft's own research and published data consistently state that MFA blocks approximately 99.9% of account-compromise attacks, making it one of the highest-value security controls available.
wrong: 50% would make MFA only marginally useful - the actual effectiveness is far higher according to Microsoft data.
75% significantly understates the documented effectiveness of MFA against automated credential attacks.
60% is not a figure cited in Microsoft or industry research for MFA effectiveness against account compromise.

questions.q: Which Microsoft Defender component acts as a Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) and discovers shadow IT?
questions.note: Defender for Cloud Apps is Microsoft's CASB - it discovers unauthorized cloud app usage (shadow IT) and enforces policies.

explain.correct: Defender for Cloud Apps is Microsoft's CASB solution. It analyzes traffic logs to discover unsanctioned cloud app usage (shadow IT), provides risk scores for those apps, and allows policy-based controls.
wrong: Defender for Office 365 protects email and collaboration tools via Safe Links and Safe Attachments - it does not perform CASB functions or cloud app discovery.
Defender for Identity monitors on-premises Active Directory for lateral movement and identity-based threats - it has no CASB capability.
Defender for Endpoint provides EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response) for device-level threats - shadow IT discovery is not its function.

questions.q: What is the function of Microsoft Purview Sensitivity Labels?
options: They block all external email automatically
They classify and encrypt content and travel with the document
They store audit logs for compliance reporting
questions.note: Sensitivity labels classify content (e.g., Confidential) and apply encryption and restrictions that stay with the file wherever it goes.

explain.correct: Microsoft Purview Sensitivity Labels classify content with labels like 'Confidential' and can apply encryption, watermarks, and access restrictions. Crucially, the label and its protections travel with the document across apps and devices.
wrong: Blocking external email is a function of mail flow rules or DLP policies in Exchange - not sensitivity labels.
Malware scanning is the function of Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Office 365 - not Purview labels.
Audit logs are managed by the Microsoft Purview Audit solution - sensitivity labels classify and protect content, they do not generate audit reports.

questions.q: Which Microsoft Purview tool BLOCKS the sharing of credit card numbers or Social Security Numbers across Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams?
questions.note: DLP policies detect sensitive data types (PII, financial info) in real time and block or warn before sharing.

explain.correct: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies in Microsoft Purview scan content in Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and endpoints for sensitive information types like credit card numbers or SSNs, then automatically block or alert on violations.
wrong: Retention Policies control how long content is kept or deleted - they do not inspect or block data sharing in real time.
Sensitivity Labels classify and protect documents - but blocking the sharing of specific data types like SSNs across workloads requires DLP policies.
eDiscovery is used to search and preserve content for legal or compliance investigations - it does not block data sharing in real time.

questions.q: What is the difference between the Microsoft Trust Center and the Service Trust Portal?
options: Trust Center is for admins; Service Trust Portal is for end users
Trust Center is a public site explaining Microsoft's commitments; Service Trust Portal requires authentication and provides SOC/ISO audit reports
Trust Center stores compliance scores; Service Trust Portal stores sensitivity labels
They are the same portal accessed from two different URLs
questions.note: Trust Center = public compliance commitments. Service Trust Portal = authenticated, has actual audit reports (SOC 1/2, ISO 27001, etc.).

explain.correct: The Trust Center (microsoft.com/trust-center) is a publicly accessible website describing Microsoft's privacy, security, and compliance commitments. The Service Trust Portal (servicetrust.microsoft.com) requires authentication and provides access to actual third-party audit reports such as SOC 1, SOC 2, and ISO 27001.
wrong: Both portals are primarily for compliance and security professionals/admins - the distinction is public vs. authenticated access, not admin vs. end-user.
Compliance scores are in Compliance Manager (inside Purview); sensitivity labels are configured in Purview - neither portal stores these.
They are distinct products with different URLs, authentication requirements, and content - they are not the same portal.

questions.q: Which Microsoft 365 plan tier caps organization size at 300 users?
options: All M365 plans cap at 300 users
questions.note: The Business plans (Basic, Standard, Premium) are designed for SMBs and cap at 300 licensed users.

explain.correct: Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Business Standard, and Business Premium all have a maximum of 300 licensed users. Organizations larger than 300 must use Enterprise plans (E3/E5) or Frontline plans (F1/F3).
wrong: E3 and E5 are enterprise plans with no user cap - they scale to tens of thousands of users.
F1 and F3 are frontline worker plans that also have no enforced 300-user cap.
Only the Business tier plans have the 300-user limit; E3, E5, F1, and F3 do not.

questions.q: Which of the following Microsoft 365 plans does NOT include Microsoft Intune for device management?
questions.note: Intune is included in Business Premium, E3, E5, and F3 - NOT in Business Basic or Business Standard.

explain.correct: Microsoft 365 Business Standard does not include Microsoft Intune. Intune (mobile device and app management) is available in Business Premium, E3, E5, and F3 plans.
wrong: Business Premium includes Intune along with Defender for Business and Entra ID P1 - it is a security-enhanced SMB plan.
E3 includes Intune as part of its enterprise management and compliance features.
F3 includes Intune for frontline worker device management, making it distinct from F1 which does not.

questions.q: Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in Microsoft Entra ID is an example of which Zero Trust principle?
questions.note: PIM grants admin rights only when needed (just-in-time) - that is the least privilege principle in action.

explain.correct: PIM implements the Zero Trust principle of 'use least privilege access' by providing just-in-time elevation of admin roles. Users have no standing admin rights; they request elevation for a limited time window when needed.
wrong: 'Assume breach' drives monitoring, incident response, and minimizing blast radius - PIM's activation model is not about assuming breach.

'Verify explicitly' means authenticating using all available signals (MFA, device compliance, location) - PIM's function is about limiting how long elevated rights exist, not the verification mechanism.
Encrypting data in transit (TLS) is a data protection mechanism, not a Zero Trust pillar that PIM addresses.

questions.q: A company wants to ensure that deleted emails in Exchange Online are preserved for litigation. Which Microsoft Purview feature should they use?
questions.note: Litigation Hold preserves mailbox content even after users delete it, making it available for eDiscovery.

explain.correct: Litigation Hold placed on an Exchange Online mailbox preserves all mailbox content - including items the user deletes - in a hidden recoverable items folder, so it remains available for legal eDiscovery requests.
wrong: Sensitivity Labels classify and protect documents - they do not preserve deleted email content for litigation.
DLP prevents the outbound sharing of sensitive data in real time - it does not preserve content already in mailboxes for legal holds.
Insider Risk Management detects and investigates risky user behavior - it does not place legal holds on mailboxes to preserve content for litigation.

questions.q: Which Microsoft 365 support option provides FREE deployment guidance to organizations with 150 or more eligible licenses?
questions.note: FastTrack is Microsoft's free onboarding and deployment benefit for eligible customers with 150+ licenses.

explain.correct: FastTrack for Microsoft 365 is a free benefit (included with eligible subscriptions) that provides remote guidance from Microsoft engineers to help organizations deploy and adopt M365 services. The minimum eligibility threshold is 150 licenses.
wrong: Microsoft Unified Support is a paid contract that provides a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) and proactive services - it is not free.
Premier Support was the predecessor to Unified Support and was also a paid, contracted offering - not a free benefit.
The self-service support portal (admin.microsoft.com) is free but provides documentation and automated troubleshooting - not guided deployment assistance from Microsoft engineers.

questions.q: Under the Microsoft Modern Lifecycle Policy, what is the MINIMUM notice Microsoft must give before removing a product feature?
questions.note: Modern Lifecycle requires at least 12 months advance notice before removing a feature that customers depend on.

explain.correct: The Microsoft Modern Lifecycle Policy requires a minimum of 12 months advance notice before Microsoft retires or removes a feature that customers need time to adapt to, giving organizations time to plan transitions.
wrong: 30 days is far too short a window for enterprise change management - Modern Lifecycle requires 12 months minimum.
6 months (180 days) is insufficient under Modern Lifecycle policy - the standard minimum is 12 months.
24 months is not the stated minimum in the Modern Lifecycle Policy - 12 months is the documented requirement.

questions.q: Which release channel delivers Microsoft 365 Apps updates twice per year, in January and July?
questions.note: Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel releases feature updates in January and July - ideal for change-averse organizations.

explain.correct: The Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel provides Microsoft 365 Apps feature updates on a predictable twice-yearly schedule, in January and July, giving IT teams maximum time to test before broad deployment.
wrong: Current Channel delivers the latest features as soon as they are ready - typically monthly or more frequently - not on a twice-yearly schedule.
Monthly Enterprise Channel delivers updates once per month on the second Tuesday - it provides more frequent updates than Semi-Annual but less frequent than Current Channel.
Targeted Release (also called First Release) is an early-adopter program within Standard or Semi-Annual release tracks - it is not a standalone Office desktop update channel.
